reason: Right category, right continent, far too early. Ore Energy, an Amsterdam-based spin-out developing iron-air batteries that store renewable power for up to 100 hours, raised €37.3 million ($43 million) in a Series A reported on 4 August 2026. Long-duration storage is a category Formula E sells into, the Netherlands gains a Season 13 round at MASCOT Zandvoort on 18-19 June 2027, and a European multi-day storage name would be a genuinely fresh signal for the desk. It fails the deal-capable test outright. A €37.3 million Series A is construction and pilot-line money for a company that has not yet built at commercial scale; a three-year Formula E team partnership at even the bottom of the market would consume a visible fraction of the round, and no Series A board approves that. For contrast, the two long-duration names the desk already carries raised at a different order of magnitude in the same window - Form Energy $750 million and Base Power $1 billion, both in August 2026 - and Antora closed $550 million in July. Ore Energy is not in their weight class yet and pitching it would waste the introduction. No case built and no team lane opened. Recommendation: keep it on the catalyst radar rather than the prospect list, and revisit at Series B or on a first commercial-scale contract - the Zandvoort round gives it a natural home stage if it gets there.
